blocks.text: Tunneled dialysis catheter placement - right IJ, antegrade tunnel

items: TDC: GlidePath 14.5 Fr; 19, 23, 27 cm tip-to-cuff lengths.
Micropuncture set: 21G needle, 0.018-inch wire, 4-5 Fr introducer.
Working wire: 0.035-inch Bentson or kit-specified wire.
Dilators (GlidePath): 8 Fr, then 10-12 Fr Dualator.
Peel-away sheath (GlidePath): 15 Fr, valved, with dilator.
Tunneler: catheter kit.
Imaging: ultrasound with sterile cover; fluoroscopy.
Sterile supplies: gloves, gown, drapes, skin prep, dressing.
Local anesthetic: lidocaine.
Scalpel: #11 blade.
Syringes: 10 mL or larger.
Lumen supplies: saline, caps, prescribed lock solution.
Neck suture: absorbable Vicryl, 3-0.
Catheter suture: nonabsorbable Prolene, 2-0.

map right IJ and carotid with ultrasound. Mark the chest exit about two fingerbreadths below the clavicle, midway between sternum and lateral clavicle; adjust to the measured catheter course and attending preference.
use maximal sterile barriers; allow skin prep to dry. Infiltrate the neck, exit site, and entire planned tunnel, tracking the total lidocaine dose.
use a #11 blade for an approximately 1 cm incision, noting attending preference. Bluntly free superficial tissue; protect the wire, vein, and catheter.
puncture under real-time ultrasound with the 21G needle. Advance the 0.018-inch wire without resistance and confirm venous course before introducing the micropuncture sheath.

through the compatible introducer, advance the selected wire under fluoroscopy into the IVC. Confirm it has not entered the right ventricle; stop for resistance or ectopy. Retain wire and introducer during tunneling.
make an approximately 1 cm incision with the #11 blade. Leave the hub external; confirm cuff position before tunneling.

flush and prepare the catheter per its instructions, then attach the tunneler securely. Pass subcutaneously from chest exit toward venotomy, tenting the skin near the neck exit. Once the tip exits the neck skin, bend the exposed tunneler away from the head to ease catheter pull-through, only if the device permits bending. Avoid deep passage, sharp turns, and wire damage.
pull through without twisting. Position the GlidePath cuff midway along the tunnel, at least 3 cm from the venous entry. Keep a smooth neck curve and the hub outside the wound.

hold the central wire and remove the micropuncture introducer. Dilate with 8 Fr, then 10-12 Fr Dualator, then place the 15 Fr valved sheath/dilator under fluoroscopy. Stop for resistance; do not blindly hub the dilator.

know whether the sheath is valved before removing its dilator. Keep the system occluded during exchanges; a valve reduces but does not eliminate air-entry risk. Coordinate respiration/ventilation with anesthesia as appropriate.

advance through the sheath under fluoroscopy, using over-wire placement only if supported by the catheter/stylet system. Peel the sheath in a controlled fashion while holding catheter position. Remove all wires/stylets and confirm the device-specific dialysis tip position, usually mid right atrium, without wall contact or kinking.
use a 10-20 mL syringe: confirm brisk blood return and easy saline flushing from each lumen. Keep hubs closed when disconnected. Poor flow: check tip position, twist, or kink.

obtain hemostasis and close the skin incision over the venotomy with 3-0 absorbable Vicryl. Take a deep-to-superficial bite, then superficial-to-deep on the opposite edge, burying the knot. Do not capture or compress the catheter.

use 2-0 nonabsorbable Prolene. Local crossed-tie technique: take an outside-to-inside skin bite superomedially, then inside-to-out inferolaterally; approximate without blanching and secure with 4 throws. Cross the tails beneath the catheter to opposite sides and tie with 4 throws; repeat the cross-and-tie with 4 throws, then a final cross-and-tie with 7 throws (4/4/4/7). Use only where compatible with the device and attending technique; otherwise use the designated suture wings. Never puncture or constrict the tubing. Recheck both lumens for easy aspiration and flushing after securement.

lock each lumen with the prescribed solution and labeled fill volume, clamp/cap per device instructions, and apply a sterile dressing. Save final fluoroscopy and document tip position, function, lock volumes, and readiness for dialysis.
confirm vein and wire before dilation; large-bore arterial cannulation needs specialist assessment before removal.
occlude open hubs and sheaths; minimize open-system time.
new ectopy warrants repositioning; avoid contact with the atrial wall or tricuspid valve.
check tip depth, kinks, thrombus, and fibrin sheath; do not force flushing or advancement.
suspected bloodstream or tunnel infection requires a specific removal/exchange and antibiotic plan, not an automatic wire exchange.
maintain wire control and release the cuff without cutting the catheter; stop traction if centrally adherent.
